newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso extends slide on U.S. long bond yield.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso extends slide on U.S. long bond yield.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended its earlier weakness against the dollar at the close of trade on Wednesday due to demand to cover short dollar positions driven by U.S. long bond higher yields, traders said.
"Some banks that were short on dollars stepped in to buy when U.S. long bonds went up," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 2.9 and 2.75 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9250/7.9290 and 7.9220/7.9250 per dollar.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 25/32 to yield 6.95 percent in late trade.
Same-day peso contracts earlier closed 4.75 centavos weaker at 7.9140/7.9190 per dollar after lagging the market.
"They got nervous when they saw stocks were down in both new York and Mexico, while U.S. long bond yields were up," another trader said. "Many had to take losses."
The Mexican bourse was down 19.82 points at 3,778.41 when the foreign exchange markets were closing in Mexico. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 88.30 points in late dealing at 7,137.02.
Dealers estimated the peso could continue to slide in the coming days on fears rises in U.S. interest rates will be announced at the May 20 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
"I feel the peso will not recover now. It has no reason to trade at less than 7.90 per dollar before the FOMC meeting," a dealer said.
